theme_scores.theme: Prison System Purpose and Statutory Framework
theme_scores.justification: Lines describing the four purposes and the need for a statutory framework are stated as objectives, not supported by any research, data, or named evidence.

Claims such as 'governors are best able to manage the circumstances of their prison' and the mention of the six reform-prison trial are asserted without any outcome data or explanation of what the trial showed.
The case for new reporting duties, league tables and accountability structures is described entirely in terms of what will be done, with no evidence offered for why this design was chosen.
'We already have data that will give us a good understanding of how prisons perform against these standards' names data but gives no explanation of what it shows or how it justifies the new measures.

theme_scores.theme: Prison Staff Training and Workforce Development
theme_scores.justification: 'Our evidence is clear...' and 'Our research suggests that prisons need to have a supportive and constructive culture' offer unnamed findings with explanation of their implications, but carry no citation.
Statements about strengthening HMIP, IMBs and the PPO describe intended changes with no evidence cited for why these specific changes are needed.

The claim that proposals are 'inspired from the success of other public sector reforms in education and health' and the ROTL '99% compliance rate' and cognitive-skills programme findings are explained as grounds for the devolved approach, but none carry a citation or link.

reasoning:
The section's core themes carry most of the weight of the argument for empowering governors, but the majority
 of them \u2013 Purpose and Statutory Framework, Governor Autonomy, Accountability and Transparency, Performance Measurement, and Inspection and Scrutiny \u2013 state intentions and structural changes ('we will overhaul how the system is configured', 'governors are best able to manage') without offering any evidence for why this particular design was chosen. The six reform-prison trial is mentioned but no outcome data accompanies it. Two core themes do better: Prison Staff Training ('Our evidence is clear: to improve prison safety we need a fundamental shift...') and especially Evidence-Based Practice and Resources, which explains that the devolution approach is 'inspired from the success of other public sector reforms in education and health' and cites the ROTL 99% compliance rate and cognitive-skills programme research on violence reduction. These reach level 1 because the evidence is explained, not just named \u2013 but none of it is cited, so a reader cannot trace or check it, keeping the whole section below level 2. Since citations are absent throughout (all <references> and <links> blocks are empty) and most core themes contain no evidence at all, the section cannot be said to show its evidence consistently across the core argument. To reach level 2 the document would need to name and cite the education/health reform evaluations and any evaluation of the six reform prisons, and link them explicitly to the governor-autonomy design.
